submission.summary:
Reviewed all 6 walk-in sore throat visits today; 5 had POSITIVE rapid strep antigen tests (pt-1026 was negative/viral - no antibiotic).

Antibiotics ordered for GAS pharyngitis (all 10-day courses):
- pt-1003 (Maria Lopez, DOB 1958-03-14): penicillin V potassium 500 mg BID. Only allergy is sulfa; beta-lactam safe.
- pt-1017 (Maria Lopez, DOB 1991-07-02): penicillin V potassium 500 mg BID. No allergies; previously tolerated amoxicillin.
- pt-1030 (Daniel King): penicillin V potassium 500 mg BID. No allergies/meds.
- pt-1021 (Jennifer Lee): cephalexin 500 mg BID. Amoxicillin allergy is a benign delayed maculopapular rash (no hives/angioedema/anaphylaxis), so a 1st-generation cephalosporin is appropriate rather than penicillin.
- pt-1023 (Elizabeth Martin): clindamycin 300 mg TID. A scanned 2015 outside urgent care record documents anaphylaxis (throat tightness, wheezing, hives, epinephrine) to penicillin VK in 2011 that was missing from her allergy list - I added "Penicillin, anaphylaxis, high criticality" to her allergy list and avoided all beta-lactams.

Note for the ordering clinicians: two different patients named Maria Lopez were seen today; orders were matched by patient id/DOB.

Reviewed all 6 walk-in sore-throat visits dated 2026-10-01. Five had POSITIVE rapid strep antigen tests (pt-1003, pt-1017, pt-1021, pt-1023, pt-1030); pt-1026 was negative (viral pharyngitis) and received no antibiotic.

Antibiotics ordered for GAS pharyngitis:
- pt-1030 (Daniel King, NKDA): amoxicillin 500 mg BID x10 days
- pt-1017 (Maria Lopez, DOB 1991-07-02, NKDA, prior amoxicillin tolerated 2023): amoxicillin 500 mg BID x10 days
- pt-1021 (Jennifer Lee): documented amoxicillin allergy is a mild delayed maculopapular rash (non-IgE, no hives/angioedema) -> cephalexin 500 mg BID x10 days
- pt-1003 (Maria Lopez, DOB 1958-03-14): 2019 outside ED record documents anaphylaxis (hives, lip/throat swelling, epinephrine) to Augmentin, not previously on the allergy list -> added high-criticality penicillin allergy and avoided all beta-lactams; azithromycin 500 mg daily x5 days
- pt-1023 (Elizabeth Martin): 2015 scanned outside record documents anaphylaxis to penicillin VK (throat tightness, wheezing, hives, epinephrine), not previously on the allergy list -> added high-criticality penicillin allergy; given concurrent sertraline (QT considerations with macrolides), chose clindamycin 300 mg TID x10 days

Chart updates: two new high-criticality penicillin allergies added (pt-1003, pt-1023). No duplicate/conflicting antibiotics were on any active med list.

Reviewed all 6 walk-in sore-throat visits from 2026-10-01. Five had POSITIVE rapid strep antigen tests (pt-1003, pt-1017, pt-1021, pt-1023, pt-1030); pt-1026 was negative (viral pharyngitis) and was not treated.

Antibiotics ordered for GAS pharyngitis:
- pt-1017 (no allergies, prior amoxicillin tolerated): amoxicillin 500 mg PO BID x10 days.
- pt-1030 (no allergies): penicillin V potassium 500 mg PO BID x10 days.
- pt-1021 (listed amoxicillin "allergy" = mild delayed maculopapular rash, no hives/angioedema): cephalexin 500 mg PO BID x10 days — non-severe delayed reaction, cephalosporin appropriate.
- pt-1003: chart review of the 2019 outside ED note revealed unlisted anaphylaxis to Augmentin (hives, lip/throat swelling, epinephrine). Added "Penicillins (amoxicillin-clavulanate)" to the allergy list (high criticality) and avoided all beta-lactams; ordered azithromycin 500 mg PO daily x5 days (no interaction with amlodipine/atorvastatin).
- pt-1023: scanned 2015 outside urgent care record documented unlisted penicillin anaphylaxis (throat tightness, wheezing, hives, epinephrine). Added "Penicillin" allergy (high criticality) and ordered azithromycin 500 mg PO daily x5 days instead of a beta-lactam.
